title: Division of 3-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Division Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Divide at least whole 3-digit by 2-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 division worksheets: dividing by multiples of 10, 3-digit by 1-digit and 2-digit numbers, remainders and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Estimate how many times the divisor fits.
key_sub: The remainder is smaller than the divisor.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To divide by a 2-digit number, estimate how many times it fits: 864 ÷ 24 → about 900 ÷ 25 = 36.
  • Use multiples of the divisor: 24, 48, 72, 96, 120 …
  • The remainder must be smaller than the divisor.
  • Check: answer × divisor + remainder = the number you divided.

Examples

Example

864 ÷ 24

24 × 30 = 720

864 − 720 = 144

24 × 6 = 144

Answer: 36

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Big remainderIf the remainder ≥ divisor, divide again.
Missing 0612 ÷ 6 = 102.
Ignoring the remainderDecide what the story needs.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about division?
faq.a: Divide at least whole 3-digit by 2-digit numbers.

faq.q: How do I check a division?
faq.a: Multiply the answer by the divisor and add the remainder.
What is left after making equal groups.

faq.q: When do I round up the answer?
faq.a: When the extra ones still need a place, like seats in a taxi.

items.q: What is 160 ÷ 20?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 160 ÷ 20 = 16 ÷ 2. 16 ÷ 2 = 8. Check: 8 × 20 = 160.

items.q: What is 450 ÷ 90?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 450 ÷ 90 = 45 ÷ 9. 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Check: 5 × 90 = 450.

items.q: What is 240 ÷ 40?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 240 ÷ 40 = 24 ÷ 4. 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Check: 6 × 40 = 240.

items.q: What is 640 ÷ 80?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 640 ÷ 80 = 64 ÷ 8. 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Check: 8 × 80 = 640.

items.q: What is 2 100 ÷ 70?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 2 100 ÷ 70 = 210 ÷ 7. 21 ÷ 7 = 3, so 210 ÷ 7 = 30. Be careful: cross out the same number of zeros in both numbers. Check: 30 × 70 = 2 100.

items.q: What is 600 ÷ 30?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 600 ÷ 30 = 60 ÷ 3. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 60 ÷ 3 = 20. Be careful: cross out the same number of zeros in both numbers. Check: 20 × 30 = 600.

items.q: What is 1 000 ÷ 50?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 1 000 ÷ 50 = 100 ÷ 5. 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so 100 ÷ 5 = 20. Be careful: 1 000 has 3 zeros, but one of them belongs to the fact 10 ÷ 5. Check: 20 × 50 = 1 000.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 70 = 3 500
items.e: Think: what number times 70 is 3 500? That is 3 500 ÷ 70 = 350 ÷ 7 = 50. Check: 50 × 70 = 3 500.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 70 = 630
items.e: Think: what number times 70 is 630? That is 630 ÷ 70 = 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Check: 9 × 70 = 630.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 80 = 1 600
items.e: Think: what number times 80 is 1 600? That is 1 600 ÷ 80 = 160 ÷ 8 = 20. Check: 20 × 80 = 1 600.

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 171 ÷ 29.
items.e: Round 29 to 30. A number close to 171 that 30 divides easily is 180, because 18 ÷ 3 = 6. 180 ÷ 30 = 6, so 171 ÷ 29 is about 6. (The exact answer is 5 R 26, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 355 ÷ 71.
items.e: Round 71 to 70. A number close to 355 that 70 divides easily is 350, because 35 ÷ 7 = 5. 350 ÷ 70 = 5, so 355 ÷ 71 is about 5. (The exact answer is 5, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 481 ÷ 67.
items.e: Round 67 to 70. A number close to 481 that 70 divides easily is 490, because 49 ÷ 7 = 7. 490 ÷ 70 = 7, so 481 ÷ 67 is about 7. (The exact answer is 7 R 12, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 1 225 ÷ 27.
items.e: Round 27 to 30. A number close to 1 225 that 30 divides easily is 1 200, because 12 ÷ 3 = 4. 1 200 ÷ 30 = 40, so 1 225 ÷ 27 is about 40. (The exact answer is 45 R 10, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 4 781 ÷ 79.
items.e: Round 79 to 80. A number close to 4 781 that 80 divides easily is 4 800, because 48 ÷ 8 = 6. 4 800 ÷ 80 = 60, so 4 781 ÷ 79 is about 60. (The exact answer is 60 R 41, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 5 564 ÷ 66.
items.e: Round 66 to 70. A number close to 5 564 that 70 divides easily is 5 600, because 56 ÷ 7 = 8. 5 600 ÷ 70 = 80, so 5 564 ÷ 66 is about 80. (The exact answer is 84 R 20, which is close.)

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 245 ÷ 78?
items.e: Round 78 to 80. Then find a number near 245 that 80 divides easily: 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so use 240 ÷ 80 = 3. 200 ÷ 80 and 250 ÷ 80 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 273 ÷ 71?
items.e: Round 71 to 70. Then find a number near 273 that 70 divides easily: 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so use 280 ÷ 70 = 4. 270 ÷ 70 and 300 ÷ 70 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 272 ÷ 74?
items.e: Round 74 to 70. Then find a number near 272 that 70 divides easily: 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so use 280 ÷ 70 = 4. 270 ÷ 70 and 300 ÷ 70 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 128 ÷ 43?
items.e: Round 43 to 40. Then find a number near 128 that 40 divides easily: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so use 120 ÷ 40 = 3. 100 ÷ 40 and 130 ÷ 40 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Answer: 29. Check: 29 × 3 = 87.

items.q: Kabelo works out 452 ÷ 4 = 110 r 2. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the quotient
He divided by the wrong number
He did not carry the remainders
items.e: Kabelo divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Answer: 113. Check: 113 × 4 = 452.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 6 = 1 r 5. Answer: 11 r 5. Check: 11 × 6 + 5 = 71.

items.q: Zanele uses short division for 854 ÷ 6. First, 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. What does she divide next?
items.e: 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2. The remainder 2 is 2 hundreds, which is 20 tens. Write it as a small 2 in front of the 5, so you divide 25 next: 25 ÷ 6 = 4 r 1. The whole answer: 142 r 2.

items.q: Lerato uses short division for 434 ÷ 3. First, 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1. What does she divide next?
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 3, so you divide 13 next: 13 ÷ 3 = 4 r 1. The whole answer: 144 r 2.

items.q: Use short division to work out 75 ÷ 3.
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Answer: 25. Check: 25 × 3 = 75.

items.q: Use short division to work out 508 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 4 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Answer: 127. Check: 127 × 4 = 508.

items.q: Ravi uses short division for 572 ÷ 4. First, 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1. What does he divide next?
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 7, so you divide 17 next: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. The whole answer: 143.

items.q: Use short division to work out 959 ÷ 7.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 7 = 3 r 4, carry the 4 to make 49; 49 ÷ 7 = 7. Answer: 137. Check: 137 × 7 = 959.

items.q: Use short division to work out 98 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 38; 38 ÷ 6 = 6 r 2. Answer: 16 r 2. Check: 16 × 6 + 2 = 98.

items.q: Use short division to work out 196 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 4 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Answer: 49. Check: 49 × 4 = 196.

items.q: Andile works out 816 ÷ 6 = 101. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the quotient
He divided by the wrong number
items.e: Andile divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 6 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer: 136. Check: 136 × 6 = 816.

items.q: Use short division to work out 943 ÷ 7.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 7 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 7 = 4 r 5. Answer: 134 r 5. Check: 134 × 7 + 5 = 943.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 38; 38 ÷ 4 = 9 r 2. Answer: 129 r 2. Check: 129 × 4 + 2 = 518.

items.q: 936 ÷ 6 = 156. Which number sentence checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 156 × 6 = 936, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 6 = 4; 6 ÷ 6 = 1. Answer: 41. Check: 41 × 6 = 246.

items.q: 708 ÷ 4 = 177. Which number sentence checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 177 × 4 = 708, which matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 7 = 9 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 7 = 1 r 6. Answer: 91 r 6. Check: 91 × 7 + 6 = 643.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 3 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Answer: 277. Check: 277 × 3 = 831.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.

What is 616 ÷ 44?
Divide.
items.e: 22 is less than 33, so start with 226. 226 ÷ 33 = 6: 6 × 33 = 198, 226 − 198 = 28. Bring down 9: 289 ÷ 33 = 8: 8 × 33 = 264, 289 − 264 = 25. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 25. Answer: 68 R 25. Check: 68 × 33 + 25 = 2 269.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 57 is less than 84, so start with 578. 578 ÷ 84 = 6: 6 × 84 = 504, 578 − 504 = 74. Bring down 5: 745 ÷ 84 = 8: 8 × 84 = 672, 745 − 672 = 73. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 73. Answer: 68 R 73. Check: 68 × 84 + 73 = 5 785.

items.q: Divide.

Work out 985 ÷ 7. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 7 = 4; 7 does not go into 5, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 5. Answer: 140 r 5. Check: 140 × 7 + 5 = 985.

items.q: Work out 82 ÷ 3. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 82 ÷ 3 = 27 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 3, so it is 13. Answer: 27 13.

items.q: What is the remainder when 646 is divided by 9?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 9 does not go into 6, so carry the 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 9 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 9 = 1 r 7. Answer: 71 r 7. Check: 71 × 9 + 7 = 646.

items.q: You divide a number by 6. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 6, the remainder can only be 1 to 5 (or 0). If you have 6 or more left, 6 goes in again.

items.q: Work out 33 ÷ 6. Give your answer as a mixed numeral in its simplest form.
items.e: 33 ÷ 6 = 5 r 3. The remainder 3 out of 6 is 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and the denominator by 3 to get 12. Answer: 5 12.

items.q: Work out 89 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 89 ÷ 4 = 22 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 4, so it is 14. Answer: 22 14.

items.q: Work out 31 ÷ 6. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 31 ÷ 6 = 5 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 6, so it is 16. Answer: 5 16.

items.q: Precious works out 263 ÷ 3 = 86 r 5. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the quotient
She did not carry the remainders
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 5 is more than 3, so 3 goes in once more: 5 − 3 = 2. The answer is 87 r 2. Check: 87 × 3 + 2 = 263.

items.q: Work out 32 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 32 ÷ 5 = 6 r 2. The remainder 2 is 2 out of 5, so it is 25. Answer: 6 25.

items.q: Work out 232 ÷ 6. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 6 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 6 = 3 r 5, carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 6 = 8 r 4. Answer: 38 r 4. Check: 38 × 6 + 4 = 232.

items.q: Work out 85 ÷ 8. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 85 ÷ 8 = 10 r 5. The remainder 5 is 5 out of 8, so it is 58. Answer: 10 58.

items.q: Work out 19 ÷ 3. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 19 ÷ 3 = 6 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 out of 3, so it is 13. Answer: 6 13.

items.q: Work out 883 ÷ 7. Give the remainder as a whole number.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 7 = 2 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 7 = 6 r 1. Answer: 126 r 1. Check: 126 × 7 + 1 = 883.

items.q: What is the remainder when 803 is divided by 7?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 7 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 7 = 4 r 5. Answer: 114 r 5. Check: 114 × 7 + 5 = 803.

items.q: Ayanda works out 163 ÷ 6 = 26 r 7. What mistake did she make?
c: She missed a 0 in the quotient
She did not carry the remainders
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 7 is more than 6, so 6 goes in once more: 7 − 6 = 1. The answer is 27 r 1. Check: 27 × 6 + 1 = 163.

items.q: Work out 37 ÷ 8. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 37 ÷ 8 = 4 r 5. The remainder 5 is 5 out of 8, so it is 58. Answer: 4 58.

items.q: Work out 83 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 83 ÷ 4 = 20 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 out of 4, so it is 34. Answer: 20 34.

items.q: Work out 956 ÷ 3. Give the remainder as a whole number.
Work out 48 ÷ 5. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 48 ÷ 5 = 9 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 out of 5, so it is 35. Answer: 9 35.

items.q: Work out 34 ÷ 4. Give your answer as a mixed numeral in its simplest form.
items.e: 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2. The remainder 2 out of 4 is 24. Simplify: divide the numerator and the denominator by 2 to get 12. Answer: 8 12.

items.q: The school library has 481 new books. Each shelf holds 9 books. How many shelves can be filled completely?
items.e: 481 ÷ 9 = 53 r 4. The 4 books left over are not enough to fill another shelf, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 53 shelves.

items.q: 94 learners are going on an excursion. Each parent’s car can take 4 learners. How many cars are needed?
items.e: 94 ÷ 4 = 23 r 2. 23 cars hold 23 × 4 = 92 learners. 2 learners still need a place, so you need 1 more: 24 cars. Round up.

items.q: A teacher shares 66 stickers equally between 7 groups. Each group gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: 66 ÷ 7 = 9 r 3. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 3 stickers.

items.q: A farm packs 69 eggs into cartons of 6. 69 ÷ 6 = 11 r 3. To find how many cartons are full, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: A carton with fewer than 6 eggs is not full, so ignore the remainder. Round down. The answer is 11 full cartons.

items.q: A coach puts 122 tennis balls into buckets of 9 and fills as many buckets as possible. How many balls are not in a bucket?
items.e: 122 ÷ 9 = 13 r 5. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 5 balls.

items.q: 86 Grade 5 learners are going on school camp. Each tent sleeps 4 learners. How many tents are needed?
items.e: 86 ÷ 4 = 21 r 2. 21 tents hold 21 × 4 = 84 learners. 2 learners still need a place, so you need 1 more: 22 tents. Round up.

items.q: At the athletics day, 92 learners line up in rows of 6 for the march past. How many learners are in the last row, which is not full?
items.e: 92 ÷ 6 = 15 r 2. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 2 learners.

items.q: A bakery has 64 lamingtons. Each box holds 6 lamingtons. How many boxes can be filled?
items.e: 64 ÷ 6 = 10 r 4. The 4 lamingtons left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 10 boxes.

items.q: 32 cakes are shared equally between 3 classes for an end-of-term party. How much cake does each class get? Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 32 ÷ 3 = 10 r 2. The 2 left-over cakes can be cut and shared too: 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Each class gets 10 23 cakes.

items.q: 242 guests are coming to the school trivia night. Each table seats 8 guests. How many tables are needed?
items.e: 242 ÷ 8 = 30 r 2. 30 tables hold 30 × 8 = 240 guests. 2 guests still need a place, so you need 1 more: 31 tables. Round up.

items.q: A farm collects 1 013 eggs. It packs them in cartons of 6. How many cartons does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 6 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 41; 41 ÷ 6 = 6 r 5, carry the 5 to make 53; 53 ÷ 6 = 8 r 5. So 1 013 ÷ 6 = 168 r 5. 168 cartons are not enough: 5 eggs would still need a carton. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 169 cartons.

items.q: Anika runs 1 936 m by running 8 laps of the school oval. Each lap is the same length. How long is one lap?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 33; 33 ÷ 8 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 8 = 2. So 1 936 ÷ 8 = 242. There is no remainder, so the answer is 242 m. Check: 242 × 8 = 1 936.

items.q: 149 learners are going to the athletics day. Each minibus has 9 seats for learners. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 9 = 1 r 5, carry the 5 to make 59; 59 ÷ 9 = 6 r 5. So 149 ÷ 9 = 16 r 5. 16 minibuses are not enough: 5 learners would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 17 minibuses.

items.q: Pieter deals 146 playing cards equally to 7 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 7 = 2; 7 does not go into 6, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 6. So 146 ÷ 7 = 20 r 6. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 6 cards.

items.q: A book has 237 pages. Chloe reads the same number of pages each day and finishes it in 3 days. How many pages does she read each day?
items.e: Divide: 3 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 3 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. So 237 ÷ 3 = 79. There is no remainder, so the answer is 79 pages. Check: 79 × 3 = 237.

items.q: 123 learners are at the athletics day. Each relay team needs exactly 4 runners. How many full relay teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3; 4 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and the remainder is 3. So 123 ÷ 4 = 30 r 3. The 3 learners left over are not enough to make another team, so round down. The answer is 30 teams.

items.q: A school orders 1 528 exercise books. They come in packs of 8. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 8 = 1 r 7, carry the 7 to make 72; 72 ÷ 8 = 9; 8 ÷ 8 = 1. So 1 528 ÷ 8 = 191. There is no remainder, so the answer is 191 packs. Check: 191 × 8 = 1 528.

items.q: A farm packs 1 799 mangoes into trays of 8. How many full trays can it pack?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 8 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 8 = 4 r 7. So 1 799 ÷ 8 = 224 r 7. The 7 mangoes left over are not enough to fill another tray, so round down. The answer is 224 trays.

items.q: A nursery has 1 834 seedlings. It plants them in trays of 6 and fills as many trays as it can. How many seedlings are not in a tray?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 6 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4. So 1 834 ÷ 6 = 305 r 4. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 seedlings.

items.q: 395 people are coming to the school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 9. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 9 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 35; 35 ÷ 9 = 3 r 8. So 395 ÷ 9 = 43 r 8. 43 rows are not enough: 8 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so round up. The answer is 44 rows.
